column1: # Rows db.x5u.* (line RG, item X5, 2026-11-20): BLASTP with unified P-values (-comp_based_stats 1u, 2u, 3u, Du) against tests/db_search/paja. NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0 adjusts a query's e-values with the length, length adjustment and search space of the next query of its batch, and for a batch's last query with bytes past its array that change from run to run. Queries tests/fasta/x5/: A = BDT63085.1 (114 residues, low entropy) and B = BDT63093.1 (85) of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa, Z = BDT63503.1 (2342) of tests/fasta/PajaWSV.faa; ab.faa [A, B], b.faa [B], z.faa [Z], a.faa [A] (psiblast's row); abx.faa [A, B, allx] (allx: 50 X), axbx.faa [A, allx310, B, allx60], ax.faa [A, allx], aba2x.faa [A, B, again_A, allx]; the copy rows' oracles (ncbi-copies:, README.md) ab_c.faa [A, B, COPY], b_c.faa [B, COPY], z_c.faa [Z, COPY], ab_c2.faa [A, COPY, B, COPY2]. The ncbi rows .abx. and .axbx. give -searchsp, so the batch's last query (no residues) has nothing to adjust and every report is NCBI's own; a copy row may take a hit-list limit (decision X5-4: NCBI's redo ends no match of a query that another query follows, and LOSAT ends none with unified P-values): c.faa [C] (C = BDT63114.1, 86 residues) and d.faa [D] (D = BDT63136.1, 985) of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa with -max_target_seqs 1 and 3 and their oracles c_c.faa, d_c.faa; alc.faa [A, lowc] (lowc: 60 Q, masked whole by -seg yes). Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --program blastp --only db.x5u. (the rows db.x5.* of blastx, tblastn and tblastx are line OF's OF4b).
